CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow up of chronic problems.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Anna is a 44-year-old female with a past medical history significant for arthritis, gout, and reflux presenting for follow up of her chronic problems. She reports that her arthritis has been improving with physical therapy and exercise. She has been doing pilates and lifting weights, which has helped build muscle and reduce joint pain. She is now able to walk about a mile to a mile and a half per day. Regarding her gout, she had an episode involving her right first big toe approximately two months ago, which responded well to medication. She is currently taking allopurinol without issues and reports no further flare-ups. Regarding her reflux, she started dietary modifications but has not completely eliminated caffeine. She continues to have some episodes with morning vomiting. She reports associated abdominal pain and bloating. Her last bowel movement was two days ago and was normal without blood. She denies weight loss, fever, or chills.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Positive for nausea, vomiting in the mornings, abdominal pain, and abdominal distension/bloating. Negative for diarrhea, weight loss, fever, chills, and blood in stool.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Arthritis, Gout, Reflux

MEDICATIONS
Omeprazole 40 milligrams once daily, Allopurinol 100 milligrams once daily

ALLERGIES
Not documented

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient exercises regularly with pilates and weight lifting.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs are within normal limits. Cardiac examination: heart sounds normal. Pulmonary examination: lungs sound clear. Abdominal examination: pain to right upper quadrant on palpation, no rebound or guarding, no peritoneal signs. Right knee examination: mild effusion, slight pain to palpation, decreased range of motion.

RESULTS
Autoimmune panel: within normal limits. Right knee x-ray: no fracture, residual arthritis present.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Reflux, nausea, and vomiting: Order right upper quadrant ultrasound to rule out gallstones. Continue omeprazole 40 milligrams once daily. Continue dietary modifications. Check labs.
2. Gout: Well controlled. Continue allopurinol 100 milligrams once daily. Refill ordered.
3. Arthritis: Improving with physical therapy. Continue pilates and use of knee. Follow up as needed for any issues; further imaging or intervention to be discussed if needed.
